newsitem.title: LEBANON: Monitors concerned at Lebanon civilian deaths.
newsitem.headline: Monitors concerned at Lebanon civilian deaths.

text.p: A five-nation group monitoring a ceasefire in Lebanon on Wednesday voiced great concern at civilian deaths in last week's cross-border violence between Israel and Lebanon.
"The Monitoring Group expressed great concern at the increasing number of serious incidents causing civilian deaths and injuries," the group said in a statement faxed to an international news agency.

The death toll at the end of last week, the bloodiest in south Lebanon since an Israeli offensive in 1996, was 15 -- seven Lebanese civilians, one Israeli soldier, a pro-Israeli Lebanese militiaman and six members of Hizbollah.

The committee comprising the United States, France, Syria, Lebanon and Israel was set up under the terms of an April 1996 U.S.-brokered ceasefire understanding which ended 17 days of an Israeli onslaught on Lebanon.
About 200 people -- mostly civilians -- were killed during the April blitz. The ceasefire understanding barred Hizbollah and Israeli troops from targeting civilians.

"The parties to the understanding unanimously committed themselves to renewed efforts to assure the full implementation of the understanding," said the statement, issued after four days of meetings at the south Lebanon coastal village of Naqoura.
The understanding, however, does not forbid Hizbollah from attacking Israeli troops and their local militia allies inside the Jewish state's south Lebanon occupation zone.

The committee, which mulled six Israeli and five Lebanese complaints, condemned Israel for two separate incidents in which Israeli shelling and air bombardment killed a total of three Lebanese civilians and wounded 12.

"The Group found that the Israeli forces were responsible for the manner in which they conducted their firing mission," the group said in reference to the Israeli air raid on Libbaya in the eastern Bekaa Valley on August 5. Two Lebanese civilians were killed and seven wounded.
"The Group determined that this action...had condemnable consequences on civilians," it added.
The group also condemned Katyusha rocketing of northern Israel. Last Friday, three rockets hit Kiryat Shmona wounding an Israeli woman.
Hizbollah, fighting to oust Israeli troops from a 15-km (nine mile)-wide south Lebanon occupation zone, said it did not fire the rockets.
"The Group called on all parties to redouble their efforts to assure compliance with all provisions of the April 26 understanding," the statement said.
"It called on responsible authorities to refrain from and prevent attacks affecting civilian-populated areas."
